title: Supabase Storage: storage.objects policies on bucket_id and storage.foldername(name)
issue: Storage policies are written over the object's path: (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text, bucket_id = '...', team folders resolved through a membership table. storage.foldername is a VOLATILE plpgsql function in Supabase, so the policy runs once per row and no index can serve it.
symptom: naive_rls and best_practice_rls evaluate the path function for every candidate row (prefix listings and counts scan whole buckets); an immutable split_part rewrite with expression indexes (best_practice_indexed_rls) fixes it. pg_auth cannot read the path: it needs a stored acl_key column derived from the path (bucket + first folder), which duplicates the policy's path rule outside the policy.

scale.meaning: number of rows in storage.objects (60% user-files, 20% team-files, 20% public-assets). users = scale/50, teams = scale/500. At 10x (1M objects): 20k users, 2k teams, ~40k team-membership rows; OpenFGA tuples = one per user folder owner + one per team membership (~60k), not per object. Generated with generate_series inserts only.
